# Runbook — Materials-manifest importer (`manifest_poll`) (an uploaded BOM or shipping log stuck / refused / dark) (Successor-Remediation, Op Stds §43)

<!-- BEGIN TREE-XREF (generated by scripts/build_runbook_xrefs.py — do not edit inside) -->
> **In the troubleshooting tree** ([printable guide](../troubleshooting/troubleshooting_guide.md) · dashboard `/troubleshoot`). This runbook resolves:
>   - Field-ops sync — portal job/hours/materials/equipment/incidents to Smartsheet → manifest-poll screens, parses, and files an uploaded BOM / shipping log → “Uploaded manifests are not being pulled or parsed.”
>   - Field-ops sync — portal job/hours/materials/equipment/incidents to Smartsheet → manifest-poll screens, parses, and files an uploaded BOM / shipping log → “An uploaded manifest was refused (unreadable, SUSPICIOUS/MALICIOUS) or failed integrity.”
> Daemon(s): `manifest-poll` — see the [daemon reference](../references/daemon_reference.md).
<!-- END TREE-XREF -->

A §43 successor-remediation entry, written for the **Successor-Operator**: a trained
operator who runs Claude Code and reads Smartsheet rows + alert emails, but does **not**
read code. Claude loads the relevant block to drive a Tier-2 repair; the operator sees the
ITS_Errors / ITS_Review_Queue / ITS_Daemon_Health evidence and approves. The §42
code-reader rationale lives in the module docstring of `field_ops/manifest_poll.py`, and
the design record is [ADR-0005](../adr/0005-materials-manifest-import.md).

`field_ops/manifest_poll.py` is part of the **generation half of the External Send Gate**
(FM v11 Invariant 1) — it is AI-free and customer-send-free. The office uploads a bill of
materials or a shipping log through the portal; the Cloudflare Worker
(`safety_portal/worker/fieldops_manifests.ts`) queues it **send-free** in D1 and signs it
(`manifest:v1`); this launchd daemon (`org.solutionsmith.its.manifest-poll`, every 120 s)
is the Mac-side consumer, behind ONE gate (`field_ops.manifest_poll.polling_enabled`).
Per document it:

1. **Claims** the row, pulls the bytes, and **verifies** them (manifest:v1 HMAC **and** a
   separate length + SHA-256 recompute) — a failure here is an INTEGRITY event
   (Symptom 4), never processed further.
2. **Screens** the document (§34 — the same screener as PO attachments and vendor
   estimates; the optional ClamAV layer reuses
   `po_materials.po_attach_screen.clamav_enabled`).
3. **Extracts the cell grid inside a killable child process.** Reading a spreadsheet or a
   PDF means running a parser over a file someone sent us, so it runs somewhere the daemon
   can kill. If that child dies or times out, the document is refused — the daemon is
   never harmed (Symptom 5).
4. **Parses** the grid, files the ORIGINAL document to Box under
   `<job>/Materials/Manifests/`, posts the grid back, and marks the manifest `parsed`.

**What it deliberately does NOT do:** it never decides which column is the quantity, and
it never commits a line. On a revision BOM there are several quantity-ish columns and the
daemon only *proposes* one; the office confirms on the validate screen. Nothing this
daemon does changes a job's material list — that happens later, when a person commits.

## What is Tier-2 and what escalates

**Tier-2 (you can do this):** re-run a cycle, read a Review-Queue row, clear a one-shot
flag to retry a *readability* refusal, ask the office for a better copy of a document,
confirm the gate and the launchd job.

**Escalates to Seth (Tier-3), always:**
- Any **integrity failure** (Symptom 4) — a signature or digest mismatch means the row or
  the bytes disagree with what was signed. Do not clear its flag.
- Any **MALICIOUS** screen verdict (Symptom 3) — it names the uploading account; that
  account is reviewed before uploads resume.
- `manifest_bearer_rejected` — a credential problem (a FIXED high-capability class).
- **Turning the gate ON for the first time** — a capability activation.

---

## Symptom 1 — "Nothing happens when the office uploads a manifest"

**Evidence:** no `manifest_poll` row in ITS_Daemon_Health, or its heartbeat is older than
~10 minutes; the manifest stays `pending` in the portal.

Two switches must BOTH be on, and a daemon with the gate off is deliberately silent — it
writes no heartbeat and no watchdog marker, because a dark lane is an intentional state,
not a fault. Check, in order:

1. **The gate.** ITS_Config → `field_ops.manifest_poll.polling_enabled`, Workstream
   `field_ops`. Read the row's **Description** as well as its value.
2. **The launchd job.** `launchctl list | grep manifest-poll`. If absent:
   `scripts/launchd/install.sh load org.solutionsmith.its.manifest-poll`.

If both are on and there is still no heartbeat, look for `manifest_creds_missing`
(CRITICAL) in ITS_Errors — see Symptom 6.

## Symptom 2 — "An upload is stuck on 'claimed'"

**Evidence:** the manifest shows `claimed` in the portal for more than a few cycles;
ITS_Errors has `manifest_transient` or `manifest_box_root_unresolved` rows for it.

`claimed` means servicing started and did not finish. **This is self-healing by design** —
the row stays serviceable and the next cycle retries it, and every step before the final
commit is safe to repeat. Nothing is lost.

- `manifest_transient` — Box or the Worker had a blip. Wait two cycles.
- `manifest_box_root_unresolved` — the Box mirror-tree root is not configured
  (`safety_reports.box.portal_root_folder_id`). The row is deliberately left unflagged so
  it files itself the moment that is set. **Escalate** if you do not know the value.

## Symptom 3 — "An upload was refused as SUSPICIOUS or MALICIOUS"

**Evidence:** an ITS_Review_Queue row with `security_flag`; ITS_Errors
`manifest_suspicious` (WARN) or `manifest_malicious` (CRITICAL).

The document was rejected by the §34 screener **before** anything was parsed or filed.
Nothing reached Box and no line was created.

- **MALICIOUS → escalate.** The alert names the uploading account. Do not clear its flag
  and do not ask for a re-upload until Seth has reviewed the account.
- **SUSPICIOUS** is usually a document with active content (a PDF with embedded
  JavaScript, a macro-enabled workbook). Ask the office to re-export it as a plain PDF or
  `.xlsx` and upload the new file. The refused one stays refused; that is correct.

## Symptom 4 — "An integrity failure alert fired" — ESCALATE

**Evidence:** ITS_Errors `manifest_integrity_failed` (CRITICAL) + a security-flagged
ITS_Review_Queue row.

The bytes or the row disagree with what the Worker signed. Deliberately, the daemon posts
**no result** for these: the bytes stay in D1 so the failure can be investigated, and the
manifest stays visible in the pool.

**Escalate to Seth. Do not clear the flag, do not retry, do not delete the manifest.**

## Symptom 5 — "A manifest was refused as unreadable"

**Evidence:** an ITS_Review_Queue row saying the document could not be imported;
ITS_Errors `manifest_unreadable` (WARN). No security flag.

This is **ordinary, not a fault**. Common causes: the PDF is a scan (an image of a table,
with no text in it), the workbook is empty or corrupt, or the export has no recognisable
header row. The Review-Queue row says what to ask for.

**Tier-2 repair:** ask the office for a text-based PDF or the source spreadsheet, and have
them upload that as a new manifest. If you believe the original was fine and want the
daemon to try again, remove that manifest's id from
`~/its/state/manifest_poll_flagged.json` — the flag exists only to stop the same alert
firing every two minutes. **Clear a flag only for a readability refusal, never for a
security verdict or an integrity failure.**

## Symptom 6 — "manifest_creds_missing (CRITICAL)" — ESCALATE

The daemon is **fail-closed**: it will not poll at all rather than run half-configured.
One of the Worker base URL, the bearer token, or the signing secret is unavailable.

A *related but different* alert, `manifest_creds_transient` (WARN), means the base URL was
briefly unreadable — a Smartsheet blip. That one clears itself; no action.

**Escalate.** Credentials are a FIXED high-capability class.

## Symptom 7 — "manifest_bearer_rejected (CRITICAL)" — ESCALATE

The daemon's token was refused (401). The cycle stops immediately rather than burning the
whole queue against a dead token, and uploads stay queued safely.

**Escalate.** Token rotation is a secrets operation.

## Symptom 8 — "manifest_pending_fetch_sustained (CRITICAL)"

The daemon could not reach the Worker for several consecutive cycles. Uploads are queueing
unserviced but nothing is lost.

**Tier-2:** check that the portal is reachable in a browser. If it is up and this persists
past a few more cycles, **escalate**.

## What "healthy" looks like

- A fresh `manifest_poll` heartbeat in ITS_Daemon_Health every ~120 s, status OK.
- Uploaded manifests moving `pending` → `claimed` → `parsed` within a cycle or two, each
  with a row count.
- The original document visible in Box under `<job>/Materials/Manifests/`.
- ITS_Errors carrying only the per-cycle `manifest_cycle_summary` INFO line.

## Go-live (Seth only)

1. Apply migration `0060` to the live D1 **before** the Worker deploys.
2. `wrangler secret put PORTAL_MANIFEST_API_TOKEN`, and store the same value in the
   Keychain as `ITS_PORTAL_MANIFEST_TOKEN`.
3. Confirm a clean run of the parser eval over the sample corpus.
4. Flip `field_ops.manifest_poll.polling_enabled` to `true` and load the launchd job.
